subject: Clarify deletion orchestration & cross-border subprocessor handoff
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@ellisdata.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@ellisdata.com
Date: Sat, 2 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deletion orchestration & subprocessor handoff — timeline and DPA questions

Hi Jonas / Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting to map our internal decommission timeline and need a tighter alignment with Redwood on three items before we can sign the DPA amendment:

1) Deletion orchestration: how Redwood coordinates the live-delete (application level), persistent store deletion, and durable backup purge. We need clearly separated windows for each stage.

2) Subprocessor transfers: Ellis runs EU-based analytics that will pull a transient copy to an EU subprocessor during migration. We need confirmation that Redwood's subprocessors will not retain copies beyond our purge windows and that any cross-border transfers are documented in the SOW.

3) Log retention exceptions: our auditors request a temporary exception window for forensic logs (up to 90 days) after the primary deletion to support investigations. Is that feasible under your standard operational playbooks?

I've attached a proposed purge timeline and our initial DPA redlines (PDF). Can you please: 1) indicate whether the attached timeline is operationally achievable, 2) flag any DPA clauses we should negotiate on subprocessor/transfer language, and 3) note any blockers for a 90-day forensic log exception?

Appreciate a short reply with concrete next steps.

Best,
Maya Singh
Director, DataOps
EllisData

Attachments: ellis_proposed_purge_timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet), ellis_dpa_redlines.pdf (PDF)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@ellisdata.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 2 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deletion orchestration & subprocessor handoff — timeline and DPA questions

Maya — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick read-through and initial answers below; we'll lock details with legal/ops early next week.

Operational feasibility (high level):
- We can support a three-stage workflow: live-delete -> persistent-store erase -> backup purge. Typical separation we run is 0–7 days between live-delete and store erase (dependent on ongoing writes) and backup purge in waves starting 14 days after store erase. Your proposed spreadsheet looks compatible with a phased purge (we'll annotate suggested buffer windows).

Subprocessor transfers and cross-border movement:
- Redwood's subprocessors are documented in the DPA addendum; any transient transfer to an EU analytics partner is allowed only if listed (or added via notice). We cannot guarantee third-party retention beyond the purge windows unless the subprocessor contract mirrors your deletion obligations. In short: Redwood will delete copies we control; we require your EU partner to commit to the same purge schedule in writing.

Log retention exception request (90-day forensic window):
- We can support a time-limited exception for specific forensic logs with three caveats: 1) the scope must be narrow (audit/forensic logs only), 2) logs must be isolated and encrypted with a distinct TTL tag, and 3) the exception must be authorized in writing by Ellis legal and Redwood security. Operationally we would implement the exception as an isolated retention bucket with an explicit expiration.

Next steps (proposed):
- Kimberley (cc) to coordinate with Redwood Legal on the DPA redlines you sent.
- Karthik (cc) to produce an annotated purge timeline and a short runbook explaining the wave purge mechanics and how KV/prefix caching interacts with deletion.
- Maya to confirm the exact log classes that require the 90-day exception.

I'll schedule a 30m call Monday to walk through the annotated timeline unless you'd prefer a written follow-up first.

—Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood_initial_annotation.xlsx]

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@ellisdata.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, legal@ellisdata.com
Date: Sun, 3 Sep 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deletion orchestration & subprocessor handoff — timeline and DPA questions

Thanks Jonas — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Scope for 90-day exception: our auditors will likely ask for (a) authentication/access logs, (b) API request traces for affected objects, and (c) anomaly detection telemetry tied to the dataset in question. We can try to narrow but expect these three classes.

- Subprocessor confirmation: Ellis will ask our EU partner to sign an addendum mirroring the purge obligations. Can Redwood provide a template clause that we can pass to them? Specifically we need a clause that:
  * requires deletion within the same purge windows,
  * prohibits long-term backups outside those windows, and
  * includes an audit right (or attestation) within 30 days of purge completion.

- Timing: we prefer the backup purge to complete within 60 days of the initial live-delete, if possible. Your phased-wave approach is okay, but can you confirm maximum wave count and the longest-tail retention in your system?

I'll be on the Monday call.

Maya
Director, DataOps, EllisData

Maya — looping in Redwood Legal and Security to close the open items. Summary of what Redwood will deliver and immediate asks from Ellis: 

What Redwood will deliver:
- A marked-up DPA addendum with specific subprocessor clause language (we will produce a template clause you can share with your EU partner).
- An annotated purge runbook (Karthik will include maximum wave count — default is 4 waves; longest-tail retention by policy is 90 days but we will configure to meet your 60-day target in the SOW).
- A secure, isolated retention bucket for narrow forensic logs with explicit TTL tagging; access will be limited to Redwood Security and Ellis-authorized contacts only.

Action items for Ellis:
- Confirm exactly which log classes (auth / API / telemetry) you want in the 90-day exception. We need a short list to scope the bucket.
- Execute the DPA addendum signoff and confirm whether you want the EU partner added as a listed subprocessor or handled via contractual attestation.

Timeline proposal:
- This week: Redwood Legal sends DPA mark-up (DocuSign link will be provided).
- Next week: Karthik publishes annotated purge runbook and wave schedule.
- Week after: Dry-run coordination for one sample dataset purge (non-production) to exercise the wave mechanics and log exception workflow.

If Ellis signs the DPA addendum and confirms log scope by EOD Friday, we can hit your 60-day purge completion target for production datasets. Otherwise we recommend the default 90-day guardrail.

I'll create a shared Drive folder with the template clause and the runbook draft and drop the DocuSign link into the folder for your legal team.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
